papers.title: A Dark-Sector Mass Flip-Flop Mechanism for the ANITA-IV Events
papers.summary: ANITA-IV has observed four upward-going air-shower candidates just below the horizon, consistent with ultra-high-energy $ν_τ$, yet IceCube, despite its much larger exposure, has detected no neutrino events at such energies. We propose a dark-sector mass flip-flop mechanism that reconciles these observations. We consider an all-sky, monoenergetic flux of ultra-high-energy $N_1$, that is lighter than its partner $N_2$ and stable in vacuum. In our scenario, an ultralight scalar mediating interactions with Earth matter inverts the mass ordering of $N_1$ and $N_2$, allowing an incident $N_1$ to decay into $N_2$ deep underground. The resulting $N_2$ propagates unimpeded through matter and exits the Earth, where the decay $N_2 \to N_1 Z'$ becomes kinematically allowed in the atmosphere, initiating an extensive air shower. At IceCube depths, neither $N_1\to N_2 Z'$ nor $N_2\to N_1 Z'$ is kinematically allowed, which explains the absence of analogous events at IceCube. Normalizing the $N_1$ flux to the four ANITA-IV events, we also predict three events during PUEO's first flight.

papers.title: Two-loop mixed QCD-EW corrections to bottom-pair production in electron-positron collisions
papers.summary: We present the two-loop mixed strong-electroweak virtual corrections to the production of a massive bottom-antibottom quark pair in electron-positron collisions. The evaluation of all the relevant Feynman integrals, including those with up to five internal massive lines with three different mass values, has been worked out relying on semi-analytical techniques, using complex-valued masses for the electroweak gauge bosons. The ultraviolet-renormalized and infrared-subtracted finite correction contributes to the NNLO QCD-EW cross section of the inclusive production of a bottom-quark pair. The methodology adopted in this calculation can be extended to the study of fully electroweak second-order corrections to benchmark precision calculations relevant to both the high-luminosity phase of the Large Hadron Collider and prospective future lepton colliders.

papers.title: Exploring the Pion Vector Form Factor Beyond the Physical Sheet
papers.summary: Using analyticity and unitarity, we parametrise the pion vector form factor on the first and second Riemann sheets, below the inelastic $πω$ threshold. We fit this model-independent parametrisation to the available $τ^-\toπ^-π^0ν_τ$ data from ALEPH, Belle, CLEO and OPAL, together with spacelike data from NA7 and JLab, and extract the pole position and couplings of the $ρ^\pm$ along with the pion charge radius and low-energy $ππ$ scattering parameters. Our results are independent of external scattering input and agree with the literature; in particular, we find $M_{ρ^\pm} = 762.07\pm 0.63$ MeV and $Γ_{ρ^\pm} = 143.62^{+0.79}_{-0.80}$ MeV. The parametrisation is publicly available in the EOS software.

papers.title: Solar Neutrinos at the ESSνSB experiment
authors: J. P. A. M. de André
papers.summary: We investigate the sensitivity of the ESSnuSB large underground water-Cherenkov (WC) detector to two key solar neutrino signatures: the MSW spectral upturn in the $^8$B electron neutrino survival probability $P_{ee}(E_ν)$, and the first direct observation of the rare hep neutrino flux. The analysis incorporates detector systematic uncertainties (energy resolution and flux normalization) and models environmental backgrounds from cosmic-ray muon spallation and $^{222}$Rn contamination. We adopt a shape-driven analysis strategy with a floating overall normalization, so that the discovery power relies on the spectral distortion rather than on the absolute event rate. In a realistic scenario with 90% spallation rejection efficiency, informed by the Super-Kamiokande experience and recent JUNO analyses, residual spallation backgrounds prevent either signal from reaching $5σ$ significance within 20 years of exposure. For the hep flux, we present a detailed sensitivity study to both its discovery and its precision, and quantify how the required spallation veto efficiency and recoil energy threshold jointly determine the achievable significance for both signals. At the adopted thresholds, discovery-level sensitivity for both signals requires approximately 99% spallation rejection over a 20-year exposure.

papers.title: Resolving Radiogenic Heterogeneity in the Earth's Mantle with Multi-Site Geo-neutrino Measurements
papers.summary: We present a global fit to geo-neutrino measurements at four underground sites (Kamioka, Gran Sasso, Sudbury, Jiangmen), combining signal rates with site-specific predictions of the lithospheric contribution to constrain the quantity and distribution of radioactivity in the Earth's mantle. Assuming a uniform distribution of radioactivity in the mantle, we find a geo-neutrino rate of $S_\text{mantle} = 14.8 \pm 4.5$ NIU when the lithospheric predictions are allowed to vary within their uncertainties. This uniform mantle signal rate corresponds to radiogenic heating of $18.5 \pm 5.6$ TW.   Although the uniform-mantle signal is resolved at $\sim3.2σ$, there is noticeable tension between the inferred mantle signals at Jiangmen and Kamioka, which may indicate non-uniform geo-neutrino production in the mantle. We explore six families of models to describe the heterogeneous spatial distribution of radiogenic elements in the Earth's mantle. Each model contains anomalous bodies or reservoirs carrying an excess of heat-producing elements over a depleted mantle (DM) background, with total inventory set by bulk-silicate-Earth mass balance and by a geochemical Th/U constraint. For each model, we compute the geo-response at each detector site and fit the resulting signals to the four measurements. A total of 968,274 individual model configurations are defined and tested. The results of $\sim$3 million distinct fits show that no plausible mantle or lithosphere model applied uniformly to all four sites reproduces the difference between the inferred mantle signals at the Jiangmen and Kamioka sites. Only local, site-specific prescriptions are able to reach the observed difference, suggesting that the Kamioka-Jiangmen tension is due to a local effect or statistical scatter, rather than large-scale mantle structure.

papers.title: Progress on the MALTA CMOS Sensor: Edge-TCT Measurements for Parametric Pixel Simulation
papers.summary: MALTA2 is a monolithic active pixel sensor, developed in the 180 nm CMOS imaging technology for radiation-hard applications in high-rate environments. This contribution summarizes recent developments in the characterization and simulation of MALTA2. The charge collection of a sensor on epitaxial silicon is studied with the Edge Transient Current Technique (Edge-TCT), using a digital readout, where the charge is reconstructed solely from binary hit data. In previous works, only specially designed analog output pixels at the matrix periphery were investigated. In contrast, the digital readout gives access to the full edge of the pixel matrix. Laser scans across neighboring pixels enable a two-dimensional parameterization of the charge collection. This parameterization serves as input to a parametric pixel simulation, which has been developed for chip design optimization and system-level studies. The simulation results are validated with test beam data.

papers.title: New measurement of BR$(K^+\rightarrowπ^+ν\barν)$ at the NA62 experiment
authors: Silvia Martellotti on behalf of NA62 Collaboration
display_authors: Silvia Martellotti on behalf of NA62 Collaboration
papers.summary: The decay $K^+\rightarrowπ^+ν\barν$ with a very precisely predicted branching ratio of less than $10^{-10}$ is one of the best candidates to reveal indirect effects of new physics at the highest mass scales. The NA62 experiment at the CERN SPS is designed to measure the branching ratio of the $K^+\rightarrowπ^+ν\barν$ decay. A new measurement of its branching ratio based on the 20230-2024 dataset is presented. This doubles the total dataset, leading to a 5$σ$ expected sensitivity for the Standard Model process.

papers.title: Probing the internal structure of the $ΩΩ$ dibaryon via its weak decays and lifetime
papers.summary: The weak decay properties of the $ΩΩ$ dibaryon play a crucial role in probing its internal structure and guiding experimental efforts. Using an effective Lagrangian approach, we systematically study its weak decays and lifetime by computing the widths for both three- and four-body final states, with amplitudes receiving contributions from single- and double-weak-vertex diagrams. We investigate the dependence of the decay properties on the binding energy ranging from a few MeV to over $100$ MeV. For weakly bound states ($E_b = 1$ and $20$ MeV), the three-body channels $ΩΛ\bar{K}$, $ΩΞπ$, and $ΞΞ\bar{K}$ exhaust essentially the entire width, with the largest channel shifting from $ΩΛ\bar{K}$ at $E_b=1$ MeV to $ΩΞπ$ at $E_b=20$ MeV. For deeply bound states ($E_b = 100$ and $120$ MeV), the $ΩΛ\bar{K}$ channel is forbidden, and the dominant modes are $ΩΞπ$ and $ΞΞ\bar{K}$, while the double-weak-vertex channel $Λ\bar{K} Λ\bar{K}$ is found to be negligibly small. As the binding energy increases, the total lifetime extends from the order of $10^{-10}~\mathrm{s}$ to $10^{-9}~\mathrm{s}$. These distinct differences in decay patterns and lifetimes provide valuable theoretical reference values for experimental searches at RHIC and the LHC, and offer a clear discriminator between the compact hexaquark and weakly bound molecular interpretations.

papers.title: Performance of the ATLAS tau trigger in Run 3 and future prospects
papers.summary: The algorithms and selections used at the trigger level in the ATLAS experiment to select events with hadronically decaying tau leptons are described. The performance of the hadronic tau trigger is presented using proton-proton collision data recorded by the ATLAS experiment in Run 3 at $\sqrt{s} = 13.6$ TeV at the Large Hadron Collider. In the plateau region of the efficiency curve for a given single tau trigger, efficiency varies between 90-98%. Correction factors for the simulated tau trigger efficiency in Monte Carlo samples were derived using 2022 and 2023 data enriched with hadronically decaying tau lepton final states, and these range from 0.95-1.05 with an uncertainty of 2-3% over a wide range of the transverse momentum of the hadronic tau candidates. In addition, potential improvements and their performance for the identification of hadronic tau candidates at trigger level are discussed using data recorded in 2026, having been implemented in selected tau trigger test chains.

papers.title: Development and Experimental Characterization of a Compact $^{228}$Th--D$_2$O Photoneutron Source for Low-Energy Nuclear Recoil Calibration
papers.summary: Calibrating the few-keV nuclear-recoil response of liquid xenon detectors calls for a low-energy neutron source. We have developed and characterized a $^{228}$Th--D$_2$O photoneutron source that converts the 2.615~MeV $γ$ rays from $^{208}$Tl into sub-MeV neutrons through the D($γ$,n)p reaction. After optimizing the D$_2$O geometry to balance neutron production against escape efficiency, we validated the chosen configuration experimentally. The forward emission rate is $1734 \pm 76~(\mathrm{stat.}) \pm 65~(\mathrm{sys.})~\mathrm{h}^{-1}$, and the spectrum unfolded from Bonner sphere data is concentrated at $0.17$--$0.22~\mathrm{MeV}$. In a 220~h exposure of PandaX-20T, the same configuration should provide about 1000 selected nuclear-recoil events. These results support the use of a long-lived $^{228}$Th--D$_2$O source for low-energy neutron calibration of large liquid xenon detectors.

papers.title: Light-Meson Spectroscopy at COMPASS
papers.summary: We report on our latest findings from studying the diffractively produced $ωπ^0π^-$, $K_S^0K^-$, and $π^-π^+π^-η$ final states and determining the associated resonance parameters. A particular focus is on the signal of the lightest hybrid meson candidate with spin-exotic quantum numbers $J^{PC}=1^{-+}$, i.e. the $π_1(1600)$, which we observe in different decay channels including $b_1(1235)π$, $f_1(1285)π$, and $η^\primeπ$. Furthermore, we highlight the observation of a supernumerary state with respect to predictions of quark models in the strange sector with $J^P=0^-$. In addition, the analysis of the non-resonant double-Regge exchange process using $η^{(\prime)}π$ data in the high-mass region is discussed. It is the first event-based likelihood fit of a double-Regge model and improves our understanding of non-resonant production mechanisms in light-meson spectroscopy.

papers.title: Multi-approach Standard Model Effective Field Theory analyses of top-quark associated production in leptonic final states at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV with the ATLAS detector
papers.summary: Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) interpretations of measurements of top-quark associated production processes in leptonic final states are presented using the full Run 2 proton-proton collision dataset recorded by the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 140 fb$^{-1}$. A simultaneous likelihood fit is performed across final states sensitive to $t\bar{t}γ$, $t\bar{t}Z$, $t\bar{t}W$, $t\bar{t}H$, $t\bar{t}t\bar{t}$, $tZq$, $tWZ$, $tHq$, and $tHW$ production, with harmonised reconstructed final-state objects and a coherent treatment of detector-level SMEFT effects across all contributing processes. Two complementary analysis strategies are investigated: an approach employing a more generic event categorisation based on counting reconstructed objects, and a more complex approach combining orthogonal regions optimised to specifically identify individual processes, as employed by previous dedicated measurements. Constraints are obtained on the Wilson coefficients of dimension-six SMEFT operators affecting top-quark interactions, including top-boson, four-quark and top-lepton operators, together with complex operator contributions. The results do not show a significant deviation from the Standard Model expectation and 95% confidence interval limits are placed in a simultaneous fit to 33 SMEFT Wilson coefficients. The comparison of the two analysis strategies provides new insight into the design of increasingly complex SMEFT interpretations. The second, more complex, approach targeting individual processes results in the best sensitivity to the majority of Wilson coefficients.

papers.title: Monopole catalysis with massive fermions: the fate of the twisted sector
papers.summary: In the massless limit a fermion scattering on the minimal $SU(5)$ monopole in the lowest partial wave produces an outgoing state with half-integer fermion number in every flavour. This state lives in a twisted sector of the Hilbert space and is now understood as an ordinary fermion attached to a topological line running back to the monopole. In the Standard Model fermion masses and confinement destroy the line at distances greater than the inverse mass scales, causing the twisted state to decay into physical asymptotic states with integer fermion numbers. We study this decay for an incoming lepton or quark of one generation. The cross-section in this partial wave saturates the unitarity bound, $σ=π/p^2$, and the energy of the outgoing state is shared among the four fermion flavours with a broad Dirichlet distribution, which sets the thresholds and the kinematics. Conservation laws allow exactly two decay channels for each incoming fermion, the helicity flip and its $(B+L)$-violating partner. For an incoming electron the $(B+L)$-violating channel is anti-nucleon synthesis, and we determine the branching ratios in two limits: the two channels are equally likely at high energy, and only the helicity flip remains at low energy, below the anti-nucleon threshold. In between we model the energy dependence. For a quark in a slow proton the $(B+L)$-violating channel is catalysed proton decay, which has no threshold and occurs with a probability close to one. Callan's statistical interpretation of the fractional state emerges in a sharper form: the state is not a superposition of two final states with equal weights, but a single state that decays into them with energy-dependent probabilities, equal only at high energy.

papers.title: Probing Ultralight Higher-spin Dark Matter using Stellar Kinematics of Dwarf Galaxies
papers.summary: Stellar kinematics of the classical Milky Way dwarf galaxies provide a powerful probe of the dark matter distribution and its underlying physics. In this article we use them to explore ultralight dark matter (ULDM) with a non-zero spin. Numerical simulations in the non-relativistic limit have shown that, for the same initial conditions, higher-spin ULDM forms a more diffuse soliton core at the galactic center, with a smoother transition to the NFW outer region, than scalar ULDM. We introduce a generalized parametrization of the ULDM halo profile that captures these spin-induced effects through three additional parameters: the normalization of the central core density, the exponent of the core-halo mass relation, and the radius of the transition to the NFW envelope. Applying this profile in a Bayesian analysis of six classical dwarf galaxies, we find halo masses in the range $10^{8.5}$-$10^{9.5}\,M_\odot$ and, from each galaxy individually, a particle mass $m \gtrsim 3\times10^{-21}$ eV. The core-halo exponent and the transition radius are consistent with their scalar values. The core-density normalization is also consistent with the scalar value in four galaxies and prefers a core denser than a scalar soliton in Fornax, while the factor-of-several suppression expected for higher-spin cores is not excluded by any single galaxy. The data therefore show no preference for the more diffuse cores of higher-spin ULDM, but do not yet rule them out.

papers.title: Three-body dynamics of the Roper resonance
papers.summary: The enigmatic Roper resonance is notoriously difficult to determine in lattice QCD. Its quantum numbers, $J^P=1/2^+$, allow for two pions and a nucleon in relative $S$-waves. This absence of a centrifugal barrier leads to strong three-body $ππN$ effects on top of the two-body $πN$ channel -maybe the reason why the Roper is obscured in lattice QCD close to physical masses. Guided by unitarity, an amplitude is constructed in which three-body states are populated through channels in $f_0(500)N(939)1/2^+$, $πΔ(1232)3/2^+$, and $πN(1440)1/2^+$ configurations. The latter channel is required by unitarity in the presence of nucleon exchange, and it contains the nucleon as a bound state, generating the $πN$ channel automatically. With the sub-channels matching the corresponding two-body amplitudes from experiment and nucleon properties, the $P_{11}$ amplitude from SAID is fitted, allowing for an accurate determination of the Roper poles close to the complex $πΔ$ threshold. The Roper poles and residues are, for the first time, determined by explicitly including this and other non-analyticities in combination with strict two- and three-body unitarity. Contour deformation allows for a direct pole search. Systematic uncertainties from the parametrization dependence are quantified. The result for the Roper $S$-matrix pole is $\sqrt{s_R}/{\rm MeV} =1346\pm 2^{+6}_{-3} - i(81\pm 2^{+7}_{-8})$. The amplitude developed here will serve as the central input for a quantization condition that allows for future determinations of the Roper resonance from lattice QCD.

papers.title: Nonperturbative Kinetic Description of the Vacuum QGP Production in the Abelian Projection Method
papers.summary: Within the framework of the Abelian projection method in the $SU(N)$ variant of QCD, a system of nonperturbative selfconsistent equations for the back-reaction problem is derived. This system describes the vacuum production of quarks under the influence of strong quasiclassical gluon fields taking into account violating of the electroneutrality condition.

papers.title: Proton Spin Fluctuation Decomposition
papers.summary: We formulate a fluctuation decomposition of proton spin in terms of the variances and covariances of the spin and orbital angular momentum of quarks and gluons. We derive their representations in terms of single- and double-parton distributions. The definite proton spin imposes sum rules requiring the variances of its spin and orbital contributions to be compensated by their covariances. This framework reveals correlations and fluctuations that are invisible to the conventional proton spin decomposition.

papers.title: Quantitative Junction Transport Modeling of RHIC Charge and Baryon Stopping
papers.summary: Charge and baryon stopping in Ru+Ru and Zr+Zr isobar collisions are modeled by HIJING with junction. With realistic nuclear geometry and a tuned diquark splitting, it reproduces STAR's net-baryon yield, charge difference, and scaled baryon-to-charge ratio at midrapidity. Junctions set the ratio's magnitude while neutron skins drive its centrality trend. At the LHC, large asymmetric pair production in HIJING obscures junction effects, causing apparent tension with data. This tuned generator reproduces RHIC data and predicts O+O behavior, setting a quantitative benchmark for baryon transport.

papers.title: Why magnetic-field effects are difficult to observe in relativistic heavy-ion collisions
papers.summary: Since a strong magnetic field is generated in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, novel phenomena have been predicted to occur in the quark-gluon plasma produced in these collisions. However, these predictions have not yet been convincingly confirmed experimentally. We reanalyze the generation and evolution of the magnetic field which plays a key role in the phenomena. Using the method of one-sided Fourier transformation, we reconcile the description in frequency and wave-vector space, which is required to properly account for the electromagnetic properties of the quark-gluon plasma, with the initial-value nature of the problem arising from the creation of the plasma medium at the moment of collision. We show that the currents induced in the quark-gluon plasma, which sustain the magnetic field, develop with a delay and are consequently less effective than usually assumed. Moreover, because the plasma initially consists predominantly of electrically neutral gluons, while charged quarks emerge at a later stage, the induced currents are further delayed. Consequently, a magnitude of the field present in the quark-gluon plasma is significantly lower than earlier estimates suggested. This may explain why magnetic-field effects are difficult to observe in relativistic heavy-ion collisions.

papers.title: Dilution of cosmological relics and gravitational waves from a supercooled electroweak phase transition in classically scale-invariant models
papers.summary: In classically scale-invariant extensions of the Standard Model the electroweak scale is generated radiatively, and the absence of tree-level mass terms keeps the symmetric phase metastable down to very low temperatures. We study the resulting phase transition in a model with a real singlet and several additional scalars coupled to the Higgs doublet and to the singlet, in which electroweak symmetry is broken along a Gildener-Weinberg flat direction and a light dilaton appears in the spectrum. Computing the bounce along the two-dimensional tunnelling path and following the false-vacuum fraction through percolation and completion, we find that the transition proceeds in a single, strongly supercooled step and completes above the QCD scale over a region of parameter space consistent with Higgs measurements and perturbativity. Despite the strong supercooling the transition is fast. The bubble walls reach their terminal velocity early, and almost all of the released vacuum energy goes into bulk motion of the plasma, which thermalises and reheats the universe close to the scale set by the vacuum energy. The resulting entropy injection dilutes pre-existing relics by up to several orders of magnitude. It raises the baryon asymmetry that must be present before the transition, relaxes the unitarity bound on the mass of thermal dark matter, and suppresses earlier gravitational-wave backgrounds. If the acoustic description of gravitational-wave production extends to this regime, the signal peaks in the millihertz band, follows an approximate scaling relation between peak amplitude and frequency set by the vacuum energy, and would be observed by LISA throughout the viable region. The results depend on the multiplicity of the new scalars and their Higgs portal coupling at leading order through a single combination, and require the singlet scale to lie at or above the TeV scale.

papers.title: A unified reduced-mass parametrization of effective chromoelectric interactions in hadrons
papers.summary: We construct a unified effective mass relation in which a common reduced-mass function describes the flavor dependence of chromoelectric pair contributions, with explicit color factors connecting $q\bar q$ and $qq$ pairs. After subtracting fixed spin-weighted chromomagnetic contributions, we jointly fit fourteen spin-averaged meson and baryon masses using constituent quark masses and an additive constant shared by both sectors, obtaining a root-mean-square (RMS) residual of 4 MeV. The fitted saturating form connects the nearly saturated light-flavor contribution with increasing attraction in the heavy-flavor region. In the common saturation limit, the leading chromoelectric contribution acts as a common mass shift for each constituent and can be absorbed into effective constituent masses; the residual pair term accounts for the flavor dependence away from saturation. With the chromomagnetic interaction included, this single parameter set reproduces the ground-state meson and baryon spectra and yields predictions for multiply heavy baryons outside the calibration set. By diagonalizing the sum of the chromoelectric and chromomagnetic mass matrices, we further obtain the ground-state spectra of $cc\bar c\bar c$, $bb\bar b\bar b$, and $bc\bar b\bar c$. The fully charmed tensor mass is ${6505}{(9)(9)}$ MeV, close to recent lattice QCD results, while the upper scalar mass of {${6562}{(9)(12)}$} MeV lies in the mass region near $X(6600)$. The tetraquark masses remain relatively stable under the examined variations of the $qq$ chromomagnetic couplings. The relative $S$-wave rearrangement-decay weights obtained from color--spin recoupling can be used to identify favored decay channels under the stated spatial-overlap approximation.

papers.title: Gauge Theory Bootstrap with varying $N_c$
papers.summary: We use the Gauge Theory Bootstrap to study asymptotically free gauge theories with a varying number of colors $N_c$. The parameter $N_c$ enters the computation through the sum rules and asymptotic form factors, allowing us to tune this microscopic parameter directly and examine the corresponding low-energy strongly coupled dynamics. For $3\le N_c\le 12$, we extract the scattering lengths, effective ranges, and low-energy constants $\bar{l}_i$, and study their $N_c$ dependence. We also obtain the $σ$, $ρ$, and $f_2$ resonances for the same range of $N_c$. The $ρ$ and $f_2$ masses depend only weakly on $N_c$, and their widths decrease as $N_c$ increases, consistent with the $1/N_c$ scaling expected for conventional $q\bar{q}$ mesons. In contrast, the $σ$ meson mass and width both increase with $N_c$, in agreement with a previous unitarized $χ$PT analysis. These results provide a further test of the Gauge Theory Bootstrap for studying asymptotically free gauge theories.

We incorporate this cross section into the equation of state of an asymmetric, self-interacting fermionic dark matter component and perform a Bayesian inference of dark matter admixed neutron stars in the two-fluid framework at $σ/m_χ= 0.1$, $1$ and $10\ {\rm cm^2/g}$. Seven nuclear matter parameters are sampled together with the dark particle mass and mass fraction, and confronted with nuclear theory and neutron star observations. The nuclear sector and the global observables are statistically indistinguishable across the whole range of cross sections, while the data constrain the dark matter mass to $m_χ\simeq 1.45-1.88$~GeV and its mass fraction to $f_χ\simeq 0.05-0.09$, depending on the cross section. Finally, comparing runs built from the same parameter draws, so that only the cross section differs, we find that it does change the baryonic radius appreciably, but only for light dark matter, a region the astrophysical data largely disfavor. The self-interaction is therefore not too weak to be seen; however its effect is hidden in the region of parameter space that the present observational data already disfavor.

Assuming a uniform distribution of radioactivity in the mantle, we find a geo-neutrino rate of $S_\text{mantle} = 14.8 \pm 4.5$ NIU when the lithospheric predictions are allowed to vary within their uncertainties. This uniform mantle signal rate corresponds to radiogenic heating of $18.5 \pm 5.6$ TW.   Although the uniform-mantle signal is resolved at $\sim3.2σ$, there is noticeable tension between the inferred mantle signals at Jiangmen and Kamioka, which may indicate non-uniform geo-neutrino production in the mantle. We explore six families of models to describe the heterogeneous spatial distribution of radiogenic elements in the Earth's mantle. Each model contains anomalous bodies or reservoirs carrying an excess of heat-producing elements over a depleted mantle (DM) background, with total inventory set by bulk-silicate-Earth mass balance and by a geochemical Th/U constraint. For each model, we compute the geo-response at each detector site and fit the resulting signals to the four measurements. A total of 968,274 individual model configurations are defined and tested. The results of $\sim$3 million distinct fits show that no plausible mantle or lithosphere model applied uniformly to all four sites reproduces the difference between the inferred mantle signals at the Jiangmen and Kamioka sites. Only local, site-specific prescriptions are able to reach the observed difference, suggesting that the Kamioka-Jiangmen tension is due to a local effect or statistical scatter, rather than large-scale mantle structure.

papers.title: Residual Entanglement vs. Residual Coherence: A Wave Packet Approach in Neutrino Oscillation with Matter
papers.summary: In this work, we investigate quantum correlations in three-flavor neutrino oscillations beyond the standard plane-wave (PW) description by employing a wave-packet formalism in the presence of constant matter density. We study three quantum correlation measures, namely the residual $l_1$-norm coherence, Concurrence Fill, and Three-$π$ entanglement, and express them in terms of transition probabilities for an initial muon-flavor state. The analysis is performed for the DUNE setup and extended beyond its baseline to study the interplay between wave-packet decoherence and matter effects over long distances. For the DUNE baseline, finite wave-packet widths suppress and smooth the oscillations relative to the PW case, with smaller widths causing stronger damping, while matter effects modify the amplitudes and positions of the oscillation features. Among the considered measures, residual $l_1$-norm coherence dominates over the entanglement measures. At very long propagation distances, wave-packet decoherence progressively washes out the oscillatory behavior, driving the oscillation probabilities and quantum correlation measures toward averaged values, with smaller wave-packet widths leading to earlier damping. Further, in the $L-δ_{\rm CP}$ plane, residual $l_1$-norm coherence exhibits weak $δ_{\rm CP}$ dependence, while Concurrence Fill and Three-$π$ entanglement show greater sensitivity at the DUNE baseline. Beyond a characteristic baseline in the extended propagation regime, all three measures approach constant values, independent of $L$ and $δ_{\rm CP}$.

papers.title: Dark matter evolution in stellar objects: A Boltzmann transport approach
papers.summary: Dark matter (DM) captured by stars offers a way to search for physics beyond the Standard Model. We study the evolution of captured DM with the Boltzmann transport equation (BTE), which follows both the abundance and the phase-space distribution of the bound particles from capture toward a stationary state. Averaging over orbital motion, we write the BTE as a master equation in energy and angular momentum that includes capture, scattering between bound orbits, annihilation and evaporation. Applying it to the Sun, we find that captured DM does not thermalize within the solar age when its scattering on nuclei is rare. The bound DM then remains much more extended than the isothermal distribution assumed in the classical treatment, and its annihilation rate can be suppressed by many orders of magnitude. We also apply the BTE to the inelastic Higgsino interpretation of the recent LUX-ZEPLIN result, which involves two DM components coupled through inelastic scattering. The thermal motion of solar nuclei opens capture channels that are closed for nuclei at rest and strengthens the constraint on the mass splitting by tens of keV.

papers.title: Next-to-leading-order QCD corrections to prompt $Υ(1S)$ pair hadroproduction
papers.summary: Working at next-to-leading order in nonrelativistic-QCD factorization, we study prompt $Υ(1S)$ pair hadroproduction, including feed-down from the excited $Υ(2S)$ and $Υ(3S)$ states and focusing on the color singlet contributions, which are known to be dominant. Besides the integrated cross section $σ^{ΥΥ}$, we predict distributions in the invariant mass $m_{ΥΥ}$, transverse momentum $p_T^{ΥΥ}$, and rapidity separation $|Δy|$ of the $Υ(1S)$ pair, as well as the one in the transverse momentum $p_T^Υ$ of either $Υ(1S)$ meson, and compare them with measurements by the CMS Collaboration at the CERN LHC with center-of-mass energies $\sqrt{s}=8$ and $13~\mathrm{TeV}$ as far as they go. The QCD corrections to $σ^{ΥΥ}$ turn out to be mildly negative, with $K$ factors of about 0.9. By contrast, the differential cross sections receive $K$ factors as small as 0.6 and 0.2 at large values of $m_{ΥΥ}\le 100$ GeV and $|Δy|\le4$, respectively, and as large as 20 for large values of $p_T^Υ\le30$ GeV. Our predictions agree well with the data, except in the outermost bins of $m_{ΥΥ}$ and $|Δy|$, where they fall short of the data, leaving room for contributions from double parton scattering as expected. Our analysis thus provides a first solid basis for the extraction of the key parameter $σ_{\mathrm{eff}}$ of double parton scattering.

papers.title: Is Spin Slow in Hot QCD?
papers.summary: Promoting spin to a hydrodynamic variable requires slow relaxation, as mass-suppressed helicity flips in hot QCD suggest. Using the full leading-order collision operator, we show instead that light-quark spin damps at the transport rate $g^4T\ln(1/g)$, nearly as fast as vector currents. Since spatial spin locks to momentum, helicity-conserving soft, small-angle scatterings readily rotate it. Damping involves multiple kinetic modes beyond a single relaxation time, global rotation adds only reversible precession, and stronger coupling further disfavors a slow spin mode in quark-gluon plasma.

papers.title: Particle diffusion in magnetized QCD matter with a realistic equation of state
papers.summary: In this study, we investigate particle number diffusion in an interacting hot QCD medium in the presence of an external magnetic field. Starting from an effective covariant description of the medium in terms of quasiparticle degrees of freedom, we employ a Chapman Enskog-like iterative expansion of the distribution function to derive the second-order relativistic magnetohydrodynamic evolution equation for the number diffusion current. The magnetic field introduces additional tensorial structures into the diffusion dynamics, thereby modifying the transport properties of the medium. We further obtain the corresponding Navier-Stokes limit and examine the influence of medium interactions and the magnetic field on the diffusion current and its associated transport coefficients. Our results show that medium interactions suppress the magnetic field-induced anisotropy in particle diffusion. This study provides a consistent framework for investigating dissipative particle transport in magnetized, interacting QCD matter and may serve as an important ingredient in developing realistic hydrodynamic descriptions of heavy-ion collisions.

papers.title: Extended $SO(10)$-inspired leptogenesis
papers.summary: We consider seesaw models with hierarchical Dirac neutrino masses. We show that, barring well known fine-tuned crossing level solutions and given current low energy neutrino experimental data, these always lead to a very hierarchical heavy neutrino spectrum. If the Dirac neutrino masses are assumed not to significantly differ from the up-quark masses, then the intermediate seesaw neutrino ($N_2$) mass falls in the correct range for its decays to explain the matter-antimatter asymmetry of the universe via ($N_2$-)leptogenesis, while the lightest seesaw neutrino decays give a negligible contribution. We show that these conclusions are valid independently of any additional condition on the Dirac neutrino mass matrix. In this way we extend the usual $SO(10)$-inspired leptogenesis scenario, assuming the mismatch between neutrino and charged lepton Dirac mass matrices at the level of the CKM matrix. We find that solutions for inverted ordered neutrino masses become viable. We still find a lower bound on the lightest neutrino mass, $m_1 \gtrsim 10^{-5}\,{\rm eV}$, but this is relaxed by two orders of magnitude. We also consider the special subset of solutions realising strong thermal leptogenesis within this extended scenario, finding that inverted ordering remains incompatible. Our results show how the emergence of the $N_2$-leptogenesis scenario within seesaw models is much more general than thought so far.

papers.title: Low-lying doubly charmed strange baryons via QCD sum rules
papers.summary: We systematically investigate the masses of the low-lying doubly heavy baryons and their $B^*(3/2^+)\to B(1/2^+)γ$ radiative transitions within QCD sum rules and light-cone sum rules (LCSR). By constructing mixed interpolating currents, we obtain $M_{Ξ_{cc}}=3.62^{+0.14}_{-0.15}$ GeV, $M_{Ξ_{cc}^*}=3.72^{+0.14}_{-0.13}$ GeV, $M_{Ω_{cc}}=3.72^{+0.13}_{-0.15}$ GeV, and $M_{Ω_{cc}^*}=3.82^{+0.13}_{-0.15}$ GeV, together with their doubly bottom partners around $10.27$--$10.34$ GeV. The extracted masses are compatible with the observed $Ξ_{cc}$ and $Ω_{cc}$ states and predict hyperfine splittings of about $101^{+27}_{-11}$ MeV and $99^{+11}_{-12}$ MeV for the $Ξ_{cc}$ and $Ω_{cc}$ systems, respectively. Using these inputs, we derive the LCSR for the electromagnetic form factors and obtain radiative widths $Γ(Ξ_{cc}^{*++}\toΞ_{cc}^{++}γ)=5.25^{+8.57}_{-3.62}$ keV, $Γ(Ξ_{cc}^{*+}\toΞ_{cc}^{+}γ)=0.31^{+0.84}_{-0.25}$ keV, and $Γ(Ω_{cc}^{*+}\toΩ_{cc}^{+}γ)=0.41^{+0.67}_{-0.30}$ keV, while the corresponding doubly bottom widths are at the $0.002$--$0.01$ keV level. We find that the magnetic-dipole contribution dominates, whereas the electric-quadrupole form factor is numerically small. The light- and heavy-quark photon-emission terms can interfere or enhance significantly, and the heavy-quark contribution cannot be neglected in radiative transitions. These results provide useful theoretical guidance for future searches for spin-$3/2$ doubly heavy baryons through radiative decay modes at LHCb, Belle II, and other experimental facilities.

papers.title: Inelastic Scalar Dark Matter in a Gauged $U(1)_{B-L}$ Model and its LZ Phenomenology
papers.summary: We study inelastic scalar dark matter (DM) in a gauged $U(1)_{B-L}$ model motivated by the high-energy recoil candidate reported by LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ). The model introduces two complex scalars, $Φ$ and $S$, charged under $U(1)_{B-L}$. The scalar $S$ is responsible for spontaneous symmetry breaking, while the two real components of $Φ$, $φ_1$ and $φ_2$, serve as DM. This two-component DM framework accommodates both exothermic and endothermic scenarios. In the exothermic scenario, the lifetime of the heavier state $φ_1$ exceeds the age of the Universe, and both states contribute to the present-day DM abundance. In the endothermic scenario, the abundance comes almost entirely from the lighter state $φ_2$. We investigate the thermal history of the dark sector and find that the two scalars have approximately equal abundances at freeze-out. We identify parameter regions that reproduce the observed relic abundance. We calculate the nuclear recoil spectra, perform a three-bin likelihood analysis, and obtain the best-fit points interpreting the LZ signal in both scenarios.

papers.title: A perturbative construction of a modular $S_3$ model for quarks
papers.summary: We present a modular-invariant supersymmetric model of flavour for quark masses and mixing, based on the group $Γ_2\cong S_3$. Hierarchies in the quark sector follow from the symmetric structure of the model, as they are generated by modular forms of different weights in the mass matrices, and no severe tuning of free superpotential coefficients is needed. Moreover, no flavons are employed besides the modulus $τ$ which is, given the gCP symmetry imposed on the model, the only source of CP violation. 8 dimensionless observables (4 mass ratios and 4 CKM parameters) are reproduced by making use of 10 free model parameters (including real and imaginary part of the modulus) within the $1σ$ range making our model, to the best of our knowledge, the $S_3$ modular model for quarks with the fewest free parameters.

papers.title: Matching lattice and continuum chiral determinants at finite volume
papers.summary: Recent formulations of lattice chiral gauge theories define a complex fermion weight either through Craig's gauge-invariant overlap measure or, following Hsu and Witten, through a continuum Weyl determinant on a reconstructed gauge connection, with its phase fixed by the five-dimensional $η$-invariant. For one $SU(5)$ generation on a flat four-torus, we prove that their relative weights agree in the continuum limit along smooth gapped paths, after fixing a normalization and subtracting a local Yang-Mills counterterm, whose coefficient we determine. On bounded smooth families a uniform Dirac gap suffices: the vacuum expansion need not converge. We obtain explicit uniform convergence rates for the logarithmic variations and, for Craig's interpolation, prove the reconstruction bounds that the matching requires, extending Hsu's small-field comparison to finite amplitude. For Hsu's reflection-positive reconstruction with flat collars, the phase variations still match, while the logarithmic coefficient of the quadratic counterterm is enhanced by a calculable, profile-dependent factor. In a hypercharge background on which the vacuum expansion diverges, numerical comparisons at the input gauge field support quadratic convergence of the phase, whereas the modulus acquires a logarithmic correction to quadratic scaling, whose coefficient follows analytically from the free overlap vacuum polarization.

papers.title: Recurrent Fourier Neural Operator for Event-by-Event Relativistic Hydrodynamics
papers.summary: Relativistic hydrodynamics is a powerful tool to simulate the evolution of the quark--gluon plasma (QGP) in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, but event-by-event simulations are computationally demanding, especially for Bayesian analyses. We develop a recurrent Fourier neural operator (rFNO) that emulates the evolution of $(2+1)$-dimensional relativistic hydrodynamics. Three networks are trained on the $32\times32$, $64\times64$, and $128\times128$ lattices using profiles of the same \textsc{VISH2+1} hydrodynamic events up to $τ-τ_0=4.8~\mathrm{fm}/c$. The networks trained on the coarser lattices are then directly evaluated on the $128\times128$ lattice without retraining, while the $128\times128$ network provides the native-resolution reference. A comparison with the \textsc{VISH2+1} results shows that the rFNO predictions across resolutions nicely capture the magnitude and structures of the temperature profiles, and describe the event-by-event eccentricities $\varepsilon_n$ ($n=2,3,4$), the momentum anisotropy $\varepsilon_p$, and their time evolution within the supervised proper-time interval. After the recurrent continuation to $τ-τ_0=6.4~\mathrm{fm}/c$, the relative errors of the predicted $\varepsilon_n$ and $\varepsilon_p$ remain within about $10\%$. These results demonstrate that the rFNO realizes zero-shot super-resolution predictions for relativistic hydrodynamics and can be recurrently continued beyond the supervised interval.

papers.title: Probing the internal structure of the $ΩΩ$ dibaryon via its weak decays and lifetime
papers.summary: The weak decay properties of the $ΩΩ$ dibaryon play a crucial role in probing its internal structure and guiding experimental efforts. Using an effective Lagrangian approach, we systematically study its weak decays and lifetime by computing the widths for both three- and four-body final states, with amplitudes receiving contributions from single- and double-weak-vertex diagrams. We investigate the dependence of the decay properties on the binding energy ranging from a few MeV to over $100$ MeV. For weakly bound states ($E_b = 1$ and $20$ MeV), the three-body channels $ΩΛ\bar{K}$, $ΩΞπ$, and $ΞΞ\bar{K}$ exhaust essentially the entire width, with the largest channel shifting from $ΩΛ\bar{K}$ at $E_b=1$ MeV to $ΩΞπ$ at $E_b=20$ MeV. For deeply bound states ($E_b = 100$ and $120$ MeV), the $ΩΛ\bar{K}$ channel is forbidden, and the dominant modes are $ΩΞπ$ and $ΞΞ\bar{K}$, while the double-weak-vertex channel $Λ\bar{K} Λ\bar{K}$ is found to be negligibly small. As the binding energy increases, the total lifetime extends from the order of $10^{-10}~\mathrm{s}$ to $10^{-9}~\mathrm{s}$. These distinct differences in decay patterns and lifetimes provide valuable theoretical reference values for experimental searches at RHIC and the LHC, and offer a clear discriminator between the compact hexaquark and weakly bound molecular interpretations.
papers.comments: 11 pages, 4 figures, comments and suggestions are welcome

papers.title: Disentangling the Effects of Phase-Specific Transport Properties on Elliptic Flow Centrality Dependence in the AMPT Model
papers.summary: The centrality dependence of charged hadron elliptic flow $v_{2}$ in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200~\rm{GeV}$ is studied using the AMPT model with phase-specific control of partonic and hadronic transport properties. By separately varying the shear viscosity $η/s$, phase transition temperature $T_{tr}$, and hadronic scattering cross sections, we isolate their distinct effects on anisotropic flow. Hadronic rescattering is found to contribute increasingly to $v_{2}$ with centrality, with the contribution becoming dominant in peripheral collisions. Scaling up hadronic cross sections by a factor of four substantially amplifies $v_{2}$ in peripheral collisions and improves agreement with STAR data, suggesting that the flattening of $v_{2}$ at high centrality may reflect a larger effective hadronic cross section and highlighting the significant role of the hadronic phase in small systems.

papers.title: Poles Are Not Enough: Zeros of Dyson-Schwinger Gluon Propagators in Yang-Mills Thermodynamics
papers.summary: A normalized two-point function with several poles does not, on its own, fix the source-free thermal partition function. For the Gaussian measure of the original gluon field, a positive-residue rational propagator contributes determinants from its poles and from zeros interlaced between them. The zero factors distinguish this completion from a gas of independent pole fields and restore two ultraviolet polarizations per adjoint eigenvalue at every finite truncation. We apply the construction to a background-covariant completion of the elliptic Dyson-Schwinger gluon kernel. The first-order SU(3) transition is already present with a single pole, and the saturated six-pole result shifts $T_c/M_g$ by only $1.48\%$, where $T_c$ is the coexistence temperature and $M_g$ is the lowest pole mass. At six poles, the zero determinants raise $T_c/M_g$ by $2.31\%$ and lower $L/T_c^4$ by $12.4\%$, where $L$ is the latent heat and each prescription uses its own $T_c$. At fixed $M_g$ the dimensional latent heat decreases by $4.0\%$. The fixed-holonomy free-energy difference gives an ultraviolet test independent of the additive pressure normalization. At fixed pole number $P$, its asymptotic value agrees with the two-polarization Weiss result when the zeros are retained and is $(3P-1)/2$ times as large in the poles-only prescription.

papers.title: High Energy Asymptotics of Quark-Gluon Correlations
papers.summary: The internal structure of the proton is encoded not only in single parton densities, but also in the quantum interference between distinct partonic configurations. We study the high energy behavior of this interference by focusing on flavor-nonsinglet quark-gluon correlations relevant to transverse spin phenomena. By establishing recursive factorization at double logarithmic accuracy in the presence of a coherent gluon insertion, we derive infrared evolution equations for the Qiu-Sterman function and its chiral odd Boer-Mulders counterpart. We find that these twist-3 functions share the leading small $x$ intercepts of their respective twist-2 counterparts, but acquire an additional $1/\ln(1/x)$ suppression due to the color structure of the coherent gluon insertion. These results may guide small $x$ extrapolations of quark-gluon correlations at the Electron Ion Collider.

papers.title: Probing the Molecular Nature of $D_{sJ}(2860)$ and $D_{s3}(2860)$ through Their Decays
papers.summary: In this work, we investigate the molecular interpretations of $D_{sJ}(2860)$ and $D_{s3}(2860)$ by studying their strong decays within the effective Lagrangian approach. We consider two possible configurations for $D_{sJ}(2860)$: an $S$-wave $D_1K$ molecule and a $P$-wave $D^*K^*$ molecule, while treating $D_{s3}(2860)$ as a $P$-wave $D^*K^*$ molecule. By fitting the LHCb-measured angular distribution and decay widths in $B_s^0\to\bar{D}^0K^-π^+$, we determine the molecular coupling constants and cutoff parameter $Λ$. Using these parameters, we calculate the total decay widths and the ratios $R$ of the partial widths into the $D^*K$ and $DK$ channels. For $D_{sJ}(2860)$, the $S$-wave $D_1K$ assignment provides a slightly better description of the measured total width than the $P$-wave $D^*K^*$ assignment. However, the combined $D_1K$ and $D^*K^*$ assignments for $D_{sJ}(2860)$ and $D_{s3}(2860)$, respectively, are disfavored by the predicted $R_{D_{s3}(2860)}$, which exceeds the experimental upper limit. In contrast, assigning both states as $P$-wave $D^*K^*$ molecules yields good agreement with the measured $R_{D_{s3}(2860)}$ and predicts $R_{D_{sJ}(2860)}\simeq 1.26$--$1.29$. These results favor the $P$-wave $D^*K^*$ molecular interpretation for both states, which can be further tested through future measurements of $R_{D_{sJ}(2860)}$.

papers.title: Connecting Electroweak Fine-Tuning, Tens-of-GeV Dark Matter, and Exotic Higgs Decays in the GNMSSM
papers.summary: In the general next-to-minimal supersymmetric standard model (GNMSSM), we connect electroweak fine-tuning, a singlino dark matter candidate with mass around tens of GeV, and Exotic Higgs Decays, identifying a natural region characterized by the mass hierarchy $m_{\tilde{S}}<m_{\tilde{B}}<m_{\tilde{H}}$ and $μ_{\rm tot}\in [200, 500]$ GeV. For fine-tuning measure $Δ\leq 40$, the branching ratio $\mathrm{Br}(h\to a_sa_s)$ falls in the range 7\%$-$25\%, with the pseudoscalar mass $m_{a_s}$ lying mostly between 10 and 20 GeV. This region splits into two viable scenarios consistent with LZ 2024 direct detection: one where the lightest CP-even Higgs $h_1$ is SM-like ($h_1$ case), and another where the second-lightest $h_2$ is SM-like ($h_2$ case). LHC searches for $h\to a_sa_s \to b\bar{b}τ^+τ^-$ exclude 12\% (10\%) of samples with 12 GeV $\leq m_{a_s} \leq$ 15.5 GeV in the $h_1$ ($h_2$) case, while a substantial fraction remains accessible at the HL-LHC in the $h_2$ case. Our analysis unifies naturalness, dark matter, and observable exotic Higgs decays, yielding concrete targets for future experiments.

papers.title: Sketching Language Models for Context Attribution
papers.summary: Context attribution asks how removing parts of a prompt changes a language model's output. We study leave-one-out (LOO) attribution for a prompt of $n$ tokens and a fixed measurement function. Computing all LOO values directly requires $n$ model evaluations. Under a stability assumption, our algorithm estimates all LOO values to error proportional to $\varepsilon$ with constant probability using $O(\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon)}/\varepsilon)$ evaluation calls. To complement our upper bound, we prove a matching $Ω(\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon)}/\varepsilon)$ lower bound on the number of evaluation calls in an oracle model. Empirically, we verify coefficient decay consistent with stability and evaluate the performance of our sketching algorithm on a small language-model retrieval task.   Technically, our result is based on a sketching algorithm for arithmetic circuits whose Taylor coefficients satisfy the stability condition recently introduced by Gunn [Gun26]. A direct adaptation of their forward differentiation sketches would require $\widetilde{O}(\log(n)/\varepsilon^2)$ evaluation calls. Our key observation is that we can apply forward differentiation to the backpropagation circuit, with only constant overhead over a forward sketch of the same Taylor degree. This reduces the variance of the sketches and is key to our improved evaluation bound. Our lower bound builds on the techniques of Amsel, Chen, Duman Keles, Halikias, Musco, and Musco [ACDH+26, SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications] for lower bounding the number of matrix-vector queries to estimate the diagonal elements of random matrices.

papers.title: Quantifying structural stability of transparent models for general insurance pricing
papers.summary: The short duration of general insurance contracts leads to rapid distributional shifts in the data, warranting regular model updates. This process may yield a post-update model that differs considerably from the pre-update model in both predictions and structure. Structural stability is upstream of predictive stability, yet existing structural stability metrics are mostly restricted to simple decision trees. Thus, we first introduce the notion of functional transparency, characterising models with a prediction function that can be expressed as a sum of univariate functions for main effects and bivariate functions for pairwise interactions. Then, we propose the Mean Squared Shape function distance, a metric to quantify the structural stability of functionally transparent models, which are particularly relevant in actuarial science. Using three public auto insurance datasets, we present a benchmark study to demonstrate the usefulness of our metric in identifying a stable and accurate transparent model. Generalised linear models with centred numerical covariates are stable, and explainable boosting machines (EBMs) offer a compromise between stability and performance. We also find that stabilisation strategies, such as sequential modelling and fixed hyperparameters, can substantially improve stability for both EBM and XGBoost models, with negligible impact on performance.

papers.title: Linear Regression with Self-Selection Bias in Polynomial Time
papers.summary: We revisit the problem of estimating $k$ linear regressors with self-selection bias in $n$ dimensions up to error $\varepsilon$ with the maximum self-selection criterion, as introduced by Cherapanamjeri, Daskalakis, Ilyas, and Zampetakis [CDIZ23, STOC]. Our main result is a $\mathrm{poly}(n,k,1/\varepsilon)$ time algorithm for the unknown-index variant of this problem, thereby improving upon the running times of the best known algorithms due to Gaitonde and Mossel [GM24] and Kalavasis, Mehrotra, and Zhou [KMZ26, COLT] with exponential dependence on $k$. Our algorithm succeeds in the presence of correlated noise between regressors, which captures the related setting of max-affine regression. Consequently, we also give the first polynomial-time algorithm for this problem, improving on the prior works of Ghosh, Pananjady, Guntuboyina, and Ramchandran [GPGR22, IEEE Transactions on Information Theory] and Gaitonde and Mossel [GM24] with exponential dependence on $k$.   Prior works exhaustively search over a $k$-dimensional subspace spanned by the regressors, using conditional moments of the response to test candidates. In contrast, our algorithm is driven by an improved understanding of the moments of the covariates. We show that, restricting to observations with large response values, the degree-$(\log n)$ Hermite moment of the covariates approximately decomposes as a sum of tensor powers of the regressors. The first step of our algorithm can be viewed as a tensor decomposition algorithm for these implicitly represented high-order tensors, which outputs unit vectors parallel to the regressors. A secondary step based on a simple variant of ordinary least squares extracts estimates for the regressors given these unit vectors. We believe our analytic insight and algorithmic components may have applications to designing efficient algorithms for other latent-variable problems.

papers.title: Introducing Feedback Delays to Non-Delayed Adversarial MDPs: Optimal $\sqrt S$ and $\sqrt K$ Dependencies in Tabular and Linear AMDPs
papers.summary: We study regret minimization in episodic Adversarial Markov Decision Processes (AMDPs) with unknown transitions and bandit feedback. In tabular AMDPs with $S$ states, $A$ actions, and horizon $H$, the best known $K$-episode regret is $\tilde O(HS\sqrt{AK})$, whose $\sqrt S$ gap to the $Ω(H\sqrt{SAK})$ lower bound has long remained open. In linear AMDPs with $d$-dimensional features, after a five-year line of improvements starting from $K^{14/15}$, computationally efficient algorithms without a simulator or exploratory assumptions still only attain $\tilde O(K^{3/4})$ regret.   A common challenge in both settings is to estimate the Q-function of a changing policy: past data comes from earlier policies that differ from (and are correlated with) the current one, while freezing the policy for future episodes worsens the dependency on $K$. We instead propose a general technique called introduced feedback delays: we estimate the Q-function of the policy using future episodes while still updating the policy, as if the feedback were delayed. While feedback delays are usually an obstacle imposed by the environment, here they are introduced voluntarily and, perhaps surprisingly, come at no extra cost. We develop Geometric Resampling with Rejection (GRR) to account for policy changes during the delay, and threshold the visitation probabilities to avoid long delays on rarely visited state-action pairs.   With this unified technique, our policy optimization algorithms achieve, with high probability, $\tilde O(\text{poly}(H)\sqrt{SAK})$ regret in tabular AMDPs, resolving the open problem; and $\tilde O(\text{poly}(d,H)\sqrt K)$ regret in linear AMDPs, giving the first efficient algorithm optimal in $K$. They also naturally extend to delayed AMDPs with a total feedback delay $\mathfrak D$, yielding the first bounds optimal in $S$ and $\mathfrak D$ (tabular) and in $K$ and $\mathfrak D$ (linear).

papers.title: Disentangling Spurious Correlations: How IRM Handles Diverse Shortcuts in Text Classification
papers.summary: In NLP, models trained via Empirical Risk Minimization (ERM) often exploit spurious correlations, such as dialectal markers, at the expense of robust linguistic features, thereby degrading their out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization. Invariant Risk Minimization (IRM) aims to suppress such shortcuts by identifying predictive relationships that remain stable across environments, but its practical utility for NLP remains debated. We use a causality-driven framework to evaluate IRM under three shortcut-generating mechanisms: label-generated features, confounding, and selection bias. Our results show that IRM successfully rejects shortcuts across the evaluated causal and anti-causal structures, including under limited environmental variation and increasing label noise. We then extend our analysis beyond controlled synthetic artifacts to two less constrained settings: gender-profession associations in Bias in Bios and semantically loaded actor-name shortcuts in ActorCorr. These experiments show that invariant learning can mitigate more realistic textual shortcuts, while semantically meaningful features require careful calibration of the invariance penalty.

papers.title: Prevalence Bounds for Edited Watermarked Text: Power Envelopes and Calibration Sensitivity
papers.summary: Watermark detectors decide whether one document came from a watermarked language model. Auditors often need a different number: the share of a corpus that did. We study this share for Gumbel-max and green-list (KGW) watermarks when every document may have been edited by an unknown amount. Without restrictions on the edits, the upper end of the identified set is 1. Combining a known least-favourable next-token distribution with a sequential coupling, we derive a power envelope indexed by three budgets: a retention floor, an entropy budget, and a budget for in-place substitutions, which for Gumbel-max make edited positions look less watermarked than human text. The envelope gives an identified set that is sharp for the alternatives it dominates, finite-sample bounds on the realized share of a fixed corpus with either the exact null or a null calibrated on an independent human sample, and confidence sequences for streams. In Gumbel-max simulations where the envelope binds, the bounds cover, and the threshold that maximizes the gap between envelope and null is generally as tight as twelve thresholds. On text from OPT-1.3B and Qwen3-1.7B, 12,000 fresh human documents scored under three keys show no robust departure from the exact null, and all bounds covered in resampling trials from finite pools of documents with random edits, substitutions and paraphrases; at a share of 0.2 the exact-null bound is about [0.14,0.38]. These results are fragile in two ways we make precise. LLM-paraphrased KGW pools fall below the envelope, yet at 2000 documents the bounds still covered in these trials. A simulated null error of 0.01, comparable to the largest deviation we observed at our thresholds, is likewise harmless at 2000 documents but breaks exact-null coverage at 100,000; a null calibrated on an independent human sample keeps coverage there, but needs a large reference sample to stay narrow.

papers.title: Temporal Regularized Learning: Self-Supervised Learning Local in Space and Time
papers.summary: Layer-local self-supervised objectives remove the backward pass between layers, but almost all still compute their loss over a batch of samples and are therefore local in space but not in time. We introduce Temporal Regularized Learning (TeReL), a spatially and temporally local learning rule for self-supervised representation learning from sequential input streams. The key idea is to instantiate a VICReg-style objective with temporally adjacent positives and non-differentiated running population statistics, yielding a per-neuron online loss with bounded state. The objective is a soft form of Slow Feature Analysis, and its gradient is a Hebbian update of the feedforward weights and an anti-Hebbian update of one lateral matrix per layer. The aim of the experiments is to show that the rule works in a small network, not to compete with backpropagation. On a class-chunked MNIST stream, a two-layer fully connected network trained with batch size one outperforms random features (96.48% versus 95.09% linear-probe accuracy) and classical SFA, and a variant that relaxes both locality constraints is comparable to supervised backpropagation. Because training and inference use the same computation, the network can keep learning from unlabeled data during inference without loss of accuracy.

papers.title: Entire sig-jump-diffusions, their expected signature and applications to score-based generative modeling
papers.summary: We develop score-based generative models for time series and standard finite-dimensional data, building on the analytical computation of the expected signature of a new class of jump-diffusions, called entire sig-jump-diffusions. These are semimartingales whose characteristics are given by linear combinations of potentially infinitely many components of their own signature. We show that their expected signature can be computed by solving linear ODEs in the extended tensor algebra, providing a tractable foundation for learning procedures. Specifically, the learning of a generalized score function for jump diffusions, a key ingredient of our generative modeling framework, can be reduced to solving linear ODEs and a deterministic optimization problem.   We further prove that polynomial jump-diffusions can be embedded into this framework, and that their expected signature reduces to a finite-dimensional system of linear ODEs. Building on this result, we develop an alternative approach for finite-dimensional data, based on inverse signature matching, a method that learns the score by matching the expected signature of the reverse process with that of the inverse forward signature.

papers.title: Uncertainty-aware quantum machine learning based on Dempster-Shafer theory
papers.summary: A large body of work in quantum machine learning has centered on characterizing the expressivity and performance of quantum models. In contrast, little attention has been paid to the reliability of predictions beyond average performance measures such as accuracy. In this work, we introduce an uncertainty-aware quantum classification framework based on Dempster-Shafer theory. This theory allows to express uncertainty through weights assigned not only to individual classification labels but to sets of labels. We introduce a training strategy that enables parameterized quantum circuits to learn such assignments directly from data. This provides an efficient way to prepare the corresponding quantum states and enables the application of different post-processing strategies. In particular, it offers a practical setting for quantum Dempster-Shafer fusion procedures with polynomial resource requirements, even when the corresponding mass functions are defined over exponentially many subsets. Overall, our work represents a step toward enabling quantum models to express uncertainty about their predictions, thereby extending the evaluation of quantum models beyond predictive performance alone.

papers.title: Stochastic Kernel Mode Decomposition: Information, Uncertainty, and Conditional Regime Inference
papers.summary: When do mode energies preserve regime information as measurement quality changes? Stochastic Kernel Mode Decomposition (sKMD) fits joint regime laws on signed KMD mode coordinates and transfers the reference mode posterior to regime probabilities and conditional reconstructions. For centered Gaussian regimes with independently varying known noise variances, fixed coordinate energies retain the full regime posterior precisely when all classes share their cross-covariances and class variances can differ only at isolated vertices of the covariance graph. We extend the characterization to nonzero means and show that freely varying correlated noise forces a fixed linear log-odds decoder to retain the full quadratic feature span even for two distinct centered regimes. At fixed quality, a three-regime example has no sufficient two-energy basis. Its smallest Bayes log-loss gap over bases of condition number at most $κ$ has sharp order $κ^{-1}$. Exact Bayes energy posteriors supply numerical gap estimates for specified bases. Additional bounds relate feature compression, independently learned mode spans and sensor-noise error to log loss. Two controlled experiments with 64 independent panels each show that signed information can improve prediction over energy summaries, while integration gives small gains over strong signed controls and depends on how the competing point rule is calibrated and how accurately observation noise is measured.

papers.title: Class-Competence Aggregation: Output-Layer Routing for Federated Multiclass DDoS Detection under Class-Concentrated Non-IID Data
papers.summary: Federated learning over distributed intrusion-detection sensors naturally produces \emph{class-concentrated} non-IID data, where an entire attack class is held by a single client and absent elsewhere. We show this collapses federated averaging in a specific, localized way: the output layer holds one decision boundary per class, and when a class's aggregation weight comes overwhelmingly from clients that have never seen it, its neuron receives an active anti-signal rather than mere dilution, collapsing to zero. On CIC-DDoS2019, standard FedAvg drives the concentrated LDAP class to $0.00 \pm 0.00\%$ F1 across every seed. We propose Class-Competence Aggregation (CCA), which aggregates the output layer per class using each client's own locally reported validation F1 as the weight, while hidden layers remain under standard size-weighted FedAvg. CCA requires no server-held auxiliary data and adds only one F1 scalar per class per round beyond the feature-scaling and class-count exchanges common to any federated pipeline. On our primary CNN-LSTM architecture, CCA alone raises LDAP F1 from $0\%$ to $84.83 \pm 1.65\%$, and the full method reaches $91.64 \pm 0.57\%$ macro F1, closing the federated-to-centralized gap from $-42.53$ to $-4.05$ points. Benchmarked against four other federated methods under identical partitions and seeds, CCA is the only one that recovers the concentrated class substantially and reliably; a $178\times$ smaller MLP shows the same qualitative recovery, though less completely, confirming the effect holds across architecture scale even as its magnitude varies. Results are validated across three seeds and replicated on a second dataset, CICIDS2017.

papers.title: On the Difficulty of Sequence-Level Supervised Learning for Autoregressive Language Models
papers.summary: During the supervised learning phase, autoregressive language models are typically trained by minimizing the negative log-likelihood of the training data, which decomposes as a sum of token-level cross-entropies via teacher forcing. This objective is simple and efficient but potentially suffers from so-called exposure bias: a mismatch between the way the model is trained and the way it is used at inference time. Can we instead design sequence-level loss functions that incorporate inference-time decoding procedures, such as greedy decoding or autoregressive sampling? We show that two natural attempts lead to loss functions that are fundamentally flawed: unbounded below. We further show that these two flawed loss functions are intimately connected: using autoregressive Gumbel tricks, the sampling based loss is the expected greedy loss under Gumbel perturbations. Since the pathology stems from the dependence of the decoded sequence on the model parameters, we analyze the update direction obtained by applying a stop gradient on the sampling procedure, leading to a moment matching direction. While it is not the gradient of any loss function, we prove that it defines a valid descent direction in function space for the autoregressive negative log-likelihood. Despite these theoretical insights, the moment matching direction suffers from high variance. We conclude that teacher forcing may well be ``all you need'' for supervised learning of autoregressive models.

papers.title: When and How SignSGD Outperforms SGD: A Functional Scaling Law Perspective
papers.summary: We study how the sign operator interacts with gradient noise to shape the learning dynamics and scaling behavior of sign-based optimizers. In power-law kernel regression with diagonal features, we establish a functional scaling law (FSL) for SignSGD under general learning rate schedules. The FSL describes the learning dynamics through two processes: signal learning and noise forgetting. The key mechanism is noise-induced preconditioning: gradient noise smooths the sign operator, inducing an effective preconditioned SGD. Noise-curvature alignment enables this preconditioning to transform the effective Hessian from $\mathbf{H}$ to $\mathbf{H}^{1/2}$. The resulting dynamics exhibit faster signal learning but slower noise forgetting than SGD. This tradeoff yields a regime-dependent comparison with SGD: (i) SignSGD achieves improved data efficiency in the hard-task regime; (ii) both optimizers achieve the same data efficiency in the easy-task regime, but SignSGD maintains this efficiency at larger batch sizes, requiring fewer optimization steps for a fixed data budget. Power-law kernel regression experiments support the proposed mechanism and predicted scaling behavior. LLM pre-training experiments further suggest that the SignSGD FSL better captures the batch-size dependence of loss dynamics for sign-based optimizers than the original SGD FSL.

papers.title: Context-Predictive Low-Rank Adaptation for Face Presentation Attack Detection
papers.summary: Face presentation attack detection requires representations that distinguish physical spoofing cues across changes in acquisition devices, subjects, and attack media. Large visual encoders offer transferable representations, but conventional binary fine-tuning supervises their final decisions without explicitly constraining how local facial evidence is represented under partial observation. We present CP-JEPA, a context-predictive adaptation framework that combines low-rank tuning of a pretrained CLIP image encoder with a joint-embedding predictive objective. A student predicts complete-image teacher features at masked spatial locations, while unmasked classification, masked classification, and prediction consistency retain the connection to the live/spoof task. An exponential-moving-average teacher supplies evolving latent targets. The auxiliary components are used only during training; inference requires only the LoRA-adapted CLIP visual encoder and binary classifier. {We evaluate CP-JEPA under single-source and multi-source OCIM transfer, additional CelebA-Spoof training, transfer to CelebA-Spoof, two-source training, and unseen-attack evaluation on SiW-Mv2.} On the standard OCIM benchmark, CP-JEPA achieves 3.74\% mean HTER and 98.73\% mean AUC. {Single-source evaluation achieves 11.36\% mean HTER across twelve source--target combinations.} With CelebA-Spoof added to the three OCIM training sources, CP-JEPA reduces mean HTER from 3.45\% to 2.35\% and increases mean AUC from 98.68\% to 99.32\%. On SiW-Mv2, it achieves 3.36\% mean HTER across the held-out attack categories. Controlled loss ablations examine the contributions of latent prediction, masked classification, and prediction consistency. The results show that context-predictive adaptation can improve cross-dataset PAD performance, although the gains vary with the training sources and evaluation setting.
